questions.question: Does the following list of numbers form an AP? Give a reason. The taxi fare after each km when the fare is ₹15 for the first km and ₹8 for each additional km.
answer_steps: Each fare is ₹8 more than the previous one, so it is an AP with $d = 8$.

questions.question:
In a class, the teacher asks every student to write an example of an AP. Two boys, Aryan and Roshan, write the progressions $-5, -2, 1, 4, \ldots$ and $187, 184, 181, \ldots$ respectively.

(i) Find the sum of the common differences of the two progressions. (1)

(ii) Find the 34th term of the progression written by Roshan. (1)

(iii) Find the sum of the first 10 terms of the progression written by Aryan. OR Which term of the two progressions will have the same value? (2)
answer_steps: (i) The common differences are $3$ and $-3$; their sum is $0$.
(iii) $S_{10} = \dfrac{10}{2}\left[2(-5) + 9 \times 3\right] = 85$. OR $-5 + (n - 1) \times 3 = 187 + (n - 1)(-3)$ gives $6(n - 1) = 192$, so the 33rd terms are equal.
